one_liner: Assesses and treats mental illness - the only psychology role India licenses.
job_roles: Clinical Psychologist | Neuropsychologist | Child & Adolescent Clinical Psychologist | Rehabilitation Psychologist | Forensic Psychologist | Psycho-diagnostician | Clinical Psychology Trainee | Community Mental Health Practitioner
entrance_exams: M.Phil Clinical Psychology entrance (RCI-recognised institutions) | CUET PG
self_emp_route: Private practice, which is the normal destination. RCI registration is what makes it lawful and what lets a practitioner charge clinical rates rather than counselling rates.
ai_reason: Very low exposure once legal accountability is applied, and the reason is the strongest in the model: a registered human must assess, decide and carry liability, and Section 13(2) of the RCI Act makes that a legal requirement rather than a convention. Psycho-diagnostician work is the most exposed - test scoring and report drafting are substantially automatable - but the signature and the responsibility cannot move.
role_spread: [Neuropsychologist, Psycho-diagnostician] higher: logical, attention_span, reasoning / lower: extraversion || [Forensic Psychologist] higher: reasoning, confidence, verbal / lower: agreeableness || [Community Mental Health Practitioner] higher: agreeableness, emotional_intelligence, naturalistic / lower: confidence
path_to_entry: class_11_12: Any stream. Psychology is available in arts, commerce and science streams and is not required at school. -> degree: BA or BSc Psychology (3-4 years). -> masters: MA or MSc in Psychology or Clinical Psychology (2 years). -> professional_qualification: M.Phil in Clinical Psychology (2 years) at an RCI-recognised institution, including supervised clinical training. THIS is the step that makes practice lawful, and places are very few. -> registration: Enrolment on the Central Rehabilitation Register. Mandatory - practising without it is an offence under Section 13 of the RCI Act.
nuances: [licensing_body] Tier A and criminally enforced. Section 13(2) of the RCI Act 1992 bars an unregistered person from practising as a clinical psychologist anywhere in India or giving expert evidence; Section 13(3) makes contravention punishable with up to a year's imprisonment. The Mental Healthcare Act 2017 defines a clinical psychologist by reference to the same RCI recognition. || [mid_stream_entry] 'after_any_degree' is technically true - the master's admission is what matters - but psychology master's programmes in practice want a psychology bachelor's, so a commerce or engineering graduate is usually restarting rather than switching. Read this as the door being open and narrow, not open and wide. || [years_to_qualify] Nine years from class 12, and the bottleneck is the last two. The M.Phil in Clinical Psychology is the only route to lawful practice and India runs very few recognised places, so a large number of psychology postgraduates never reach it and work unregistered as counsellors instead. || [demand_signal] High and severely undersupplied - India has a very small number of registered clinical psychologists for its population. The shortage does not translate into easy entry, because the constraint is M.Phil seats rather than demand.

one_liner: Talks people through difficulty - the mental health work India does not regulate at all.
job_roles: Counsellor | Psychotherapist | School Counsellor | Career & Student Counsellor | Marriage & Family Counsellor | Addiction & De-addiction Counsellor | Genetic Counsellor | Grief & Trauma Counsellor | Helpline Counsellor | Workplace Wellbeing Counsellor | Music & Arts Therapist
entrance_exams: CUET UG | CUET PG | Counselling and psychotherapy diplomas (private providers)
self_emp_route: Private practice, seen either online or from a room, charging per session. Entry requires nothing but a client, which is both why the profession is accessible and why it is unsafe.
ai_reason: Clarity-heavy, and the band was raised to medium on the second pass because a low band contradicted this very paragraph. A counselling conversation IS output a model can produce, which is what skill_digital measures, and pretending otherwise understated the one profession here where AI competes with the SERVICE rather than the admin around it. This is the profession where AI chat products compete most directly with the service itself rather than with the work around it. Helpline Counsellor and Workplace Wellbeing Counsellor face that first, since both are single-contact and text-mediated. Marriage & Family Counsellor and Addiction & De-addiction Counsellor are protected by the work being relational and confrontational over months.
role_spread: [Genetic Counsellor] higher: logical, reasoning, conscientiousness / lower: openness || [Addiction & De-addiction Counsellor] higher: confidence, conscientiousness / lower: agreeableness, emotional_stability || [Helpline Counsellor] higher: emotional_intelligence, short_term_memory, verbal / lower: long_term_memory
path_to_entry: class_11_12: Any stream. -> degree: Usually a BA or BSc in Psychology, then an MA or MSc. Nothing is legally required, which is the defining fact about this profession. -> training: A counselling or psychotherapy diploma and supervised practice hours. Reputable, entirely voluntary, and not verifiable by a client. -> work: School counselling cell, NGO, helpline, de-addiction centre, corporate wellbeing programme, or private practice.
nuances: [licensing_body] Null, and it is the most important thing on this record. The titles 'counsellor' and 'psychotherapist' carry NO statutory register in India - the RCI Act does not list a general counsellor among rehabilitation professionals. Anyone may use the title and charge for therapy. Association membership is not registration, and a client cannot tell the difference from a job title. || [profession] Deliberately separated from Clinical Psychologist rather than merged, despite overlapping work. The two share an object of concern and much of a skill set, which would normally trigger the merge test in DECISIONS.md 8.95 - but one is Tier A with criminal enforcement and a nine-year runway, and the other has no gate at all. Merging them would hide exactly the distinction a student and a client most need. || [economics] Sits below Clinical Psychologist for the same reason it is easier to enter: no registration means no protected scope, so rates are set by an open market with no floor. Practitioners who also hold an RCI registration charge clinical rates; those who do not, compete on price.

one_liner: Works with people the system is failing - families, children, patients, the displaced.
job_roles: Social Worker | Medical & Psychiatric Social Worker | Child Welfare Officer | Probation Officer | Community Social Worker | Disaster Response & Relief Worker | Rehabilitation Social Worker | Case Worker | School Social Worker | Social Worker (Government Schemes)
entrance_exams: CUET PG | TISS and central university MSW admissions | State recruitment for Probation and Child Welfare Officer posts
self_emp_route: Independent consultancy to NGOs and funders on programme design, safeguarding and evaluation, usually after ten years in the field.
ai_reason: Low exposure. The work is being physically present with people in difficulty, in homes, hospitals, shelters and courts, and holding a case over months. Case Worker documentation and reporting is the exposed part and it is real - social workers spend a great deal of time on records - but automating the paperwork frees the job rather than removing it.
role_spread: [Medical & Psychiatric Social Worker] higher: emotional_intelligence, conscientiousness, reasoning / lower: bodily || [Disaster Response & Relief Worker] higher: bodily, confidence / lower: attention_span, emotional_stability || [Probation Officer, Child Welfare Officer] higher: conscientiousness, logical, confidence / lower: agreeableness
path_to_entry: class_11_12: Any stream. -> degree: BSW, or any bachelor's degree followed by an MSW. The MSW is what the field actually recruits on. -> fieldwork: Supervised fieldwork placements, which are built into the MSW and are where employability is decided. -> work: NGO, hospital, government department, corporate CSR team, or a statutory post such as Probation Officer.
nuances: [job_roles] Psychiatric social work has an RCI-recognised M.Phil route and therefore falls under the same Act as clinical psychology, unlike the rest of this profession. A student intending hospital mental health work should read the Clinical Psychologist record alongside this one. || [entry_competition] Null, and deliberately so. MSW admission is the practical gate and it now runs largely through CUET PG - but pointing this record at CUET UG would repeat the mistake corrected in Sector 3, telling a would-be social worker that the hard part is getting into a bachelor's degree. It is not. The MSW admission is in pending_gates. || [economics] Split by employer rather than by ability. A statutory government post - Probation Officer, Child Welfare Officer - carries a pay scale and a pension; the NGO sector pays modestly and on project funding cycles; corporate CSR pays best and employs fewest. The same MSW leads to all three. || [demand_signal] Moderate, and it depends on funding rather than need. The need is enormous and constant; the number of funded posts moves with government scheme budgets and CSR compliance, which is a different signal entirely.

one_liner: Designs and runs programmes meant to change something - poverty, health, education, rights.
job_roles: Programme Officer | Project Coordinator (Development) | Livelihoods Specialist | Field Officer | Fundraising & Grants Officer | CSR Officer | Advocacy & Campaigns Officer | Partnerships Manager (Development) | Programme Documentation Officer
entrance_exams: CUET PG | IRMA and rural management entrances | CAT | Development fellowships (Gandhi Fellowship, PMRDF and others)
self_emp_route: Independent consultancy to NGOs, funders and government programmes - programme design, evaluation and proposal writing. Common after eight to ten years and generally better paid than the salaried version.
ai_reason: Moderately exposed on the paperwork and protected on the ground. Programme Documentation Officer and much of Fundraising & Grants Officer work - proposals, donor reports, log frames - is templated writing that generates well, and that is a large share of the sector's desk time. Field Officer and Advocacy & Campaigns Officer are protected by needing to be in a village or a room with people who can say no.
role_spread: [Fundraising & Grants Officer, Partnerships Manager (Development)] higher: verbal, extraversion, conscientiousness / lower: naturalistic || [Field Officer] higher: bodily, agreeableness, naturalistic / lower: logical || [Advocacy & Campaigns Officer] higher: verbal, confidence, openness / lower: agreeableness
path_to_entry: class_11_12: Any stream. -> degree: Any bachelor's degree. MSW, development studies, rural management (IRMA), public policy and economics are all common routes in. -> field_exposure: A fellowship or field stint - Gandhi Fellowship, Prime Minister's Rural Development Fellows, SBI Youth for India and similar. This is how most people actually enter. -> work: NGO, foundation, multilateral agency, government programme unit, or a corporate CSR team.
nuances: [demand_signal] Moderate and structurally unstable. Employment here follows grant cycles, CSR compliance and government scheme budgets rather than the underlying problem, so posts appear and vanish on two-to-three-year project timelines. That instability is the profession's defining employment characteristic and is invisible in a salary range. || [demand_signal] Pathway is 'any' because this is one of the few Indian professions with a genuine international ladder that does not require emigration - multilateral agencies, international NGOs and global foundations recruit in India for regional roles.

one_liner: Measures whether a social programme actually worked, and says so when it did not.
job_roles: Monitoring & Evaluation Officer | Impact Assessment Analyst | Research Associate (Development) | Survey & Field Research Coordinator | Data Analyst (Development) | Randomised Evaluation Field Manager | MIS & Reporting Analyst | Social Audit Facilitator
entrance_exams: CUET PG | Master's in economics and public policy admissions
self_emp_route: Independent evaluation consultancy, which is a real market - funders increasingly require third-party evaluation, and an evaluator's independence is the product.
ai_reason: The most exposed profession in this sector. MIS & Reporting Analyst and Data Analyst (Development) do work that is directly substitutable - cleaning, tabulating and charting survey data - and much of routine M&E reporting is already automated in dashboards. What survives is study design and the willingness to report a null result: deciding what would count as evidence that a programme failed, and saying so to the people who funded it.
role_spread: [Randomised Evaluation Field Manager, Survey & Field Research Coordinator] higher: conscientiousness, extraversion, attention_span / lower: openness || [Social Audit Facilitator] higher: confidence, verbal, agreeableness / lower: logical
path_to_entry: class_11_12: Any stream. Mathematics helps substantially and is not required. -> degree: Economics, statistics, development studies, public policy or social sciences. The quantitative half of this job is what makes it distinct. -> work: Research associate at a research organisation, an evaluation firm or an NGO's M&E unit. This is a recognised entry job with a defined skill test. -> specialisation: Impact evaluation, survey methods or programme MIS. The first transfers to economics research and academia.
nuances: [profession] Kept separate from Development & Programme Professional rather than folded in as job roles. They share an object of concern but not a skill set - this is quantitative research method, survey design and statistics, and the merge test in DECISIONS.md 8.95 turns on the skill set being separate. || [industrial_sectors] Tagged EXT-RND as well as EXT-DEV. The boundary with Sector 3 is the one DECISIONS.md 2 draws by METHOD rather than discipline: this is empirical, quantitative work, and it sits here only because its object of concern is whether an intervention helped rather than what is true in general.

one_liner: Organises people in a village or neighbourhood to claim services and run things themselves.
job_roles: Community Mobiliser | Self-Help Group Facilitator | Village Level Entrepreneur | Panchayat Support Worker | Livelihoods Field Worker | Cluster Coordinator | Community Resource Person | Block Programme Assistant
self_emp_route: A village-level enterprise on commission - common service centre, banking correspondent, agri-input or insurance agency. This is the realistic route above a programme honorarium, and it is a business rather than a promotion.
ai_reason: Almost unexposed. The work is walking to households, holding meetings, and being a person the village already knows and trusts. Block Programme Assistant carries the only meaningful exposure, through scheme reporting that has largely moved onto phone applications - which has changed the job rather than removed it.
role_spread: [Village Level Entrepreneur] higher: confidence, logical, extraversion / lower: agreeableness || [Cluster Coordinator, Block Programme Assistant] higher: conscientiousness, verbal, attention_span / lower: bodily
path_to_entry: class_11_12: Class 10 or 12. Many roles specify residence in the block or village as a condition. -> training: Programme induction training, usually run by the implementing agency or the state rural livelihoods mission. -> work: State rural livelihoods mission, an NGO project, a self-help group federation, or a scheme delivery unit. -> progression: Cluster or block coordination, or running a village-level enterprise on commission.
review_reason: No sourced figure for community worker honoraria or for the commission a village level entrepreneur earns, and the second is the entire route out of a 2.7 LPA ceiling. Both vary by state and by scheme, which is exactly why an unsourced national range is close to meaningless here.
nuances: [economics] The base layer of the development sector, and it fails the compensation filter. Most of these roles are paid a project honorarium or a per-activity incentive rather than a salary, on contracts tied to a scheme's funding period. There is no pay scale and usually no notice period. || [demand_signal] Moderate and geographically inverted relative to most of this dataset - these posts exist in rural blocks and small towns and barely exist in metros. For a student outside a city this is often the only formal development-sector entry available locally.

one_liner: Makes work, buildings and services usable by disabled people, and supports them into them.
job_roles: Vocational Rehabilitation Counsellor | Disability Rights Officer | Accessibility Auditor | Assistive Technology Specialist | Multi-purpose Rehabilitation Worker | Community Based Rehabilitation Worker | Inclusive Employment Specialist | Sign Language Interpreter
self_emp_route: Independent accessibility auditing and inclusion consultancy, which has become a real market since the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act 2016 made compliance a legal obligation for employers and public buildings.
ai_reason: Low exposure with an unusual twist: the technologies that automate parts of this profession are the same ones that expand what disabled people can do independently. Sign Language Interpreter faces genuine competition from automated interpretation, though Indian Sign Language is poorly resourced and that is some way off. Community Based Rehabilitation Worker and Vocational Rehabilitation Counsellor are protected by home visits and by RCI accountability.
role_spread: [Accessibility Auditor, Assistive Technology Specialist] higher: spatial, logical, attention_span / lower: extraversion || [Sign Language Interpreter] higher: bodily, short_term_memory, verbal / lower: openness || [Community Based Rehabilitation Worker] higher: agreeableness, bodily, naturalistic / lower: logical
path_to_entry: class_11_12: Any stream. -> degree: A bachelor's degree, then an RCI-recognised qualification for the rehabilitation roles, or a specialist course for interpreting and accessibility. -> registration: Enrolment on the Central Rehabilitation Register IF the role is one the RCI Act lists - vocational counsellors and multi-purpose rehabilitation workers are listed; accessibility auditors are not. -> work: Disability NGO, a national institute, a state disability commissioner's office, a company's inclusion team, or an accessibility consultancy.
nuances: [licensing_body] Null at the profession level, but NOT for every role inside it. The RCI Act lists vocational counsellors and employment officers dealing with the handicapped, and multi-purpose rehabilitation workers, among rehabilitation professionals - those require Central Rehabilitation Register enrolment. Accessibility Auditor and Sign Language Interpreter do not. A student must check which role they are entering. || [demand_signal] Moderate and rising for a specific legal reason: the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act 2016 places obligations on employers, public buildings and services, which created a compliance market where there had been only charity.

one_liner: Protects children at risk - abuse, trafficking, child labour, adoption and institutional care.
job_roles: Child Protection Officer | Child Welfare Committee Support Officer | Childline Coordinator | Adoption & Foster Care Officer | Legal-cum-Probation Officer | Superintendent (Child Care Institution) | Outreach Worker (Children at Risk) | POCSO Support Person
entrance_exams: State District Child Protection Unit recruitment | CUET PG
ai_reason: Very low exposure. The work is interviewing frightened children, judging whether a home is safe, and being personally answerable under the Juvenile Justice Act and POCSO for a decision about a child's life. Case documentation is the only exposed part, and it is documentation that a court will read.
role_spread: [POCSO Support Person, Legal-cum-Probation Officer] higher: confidence, verbal, conscientiousness, emotional_stability / lower: - || [Outreach Worker (Children at Risk)] higher: bodily, confidence, agreeableness / lower: attention_span
path_to_entry: class_11_12: Any stream. -> degree: MSW, psychology, sociology, child development or law. Statutory posts specify qualifications and experience with children. -> work: District Child Protection Unit, a Child Care Institution, Childline, or a child rights NGO. -> statutory_post: Appointment to a statutory role under the Juvenile Justice Act or POCSO framework, which carries defined legal duties.
nuances: [ai_exposure] legal_accountability is true without a licensing body, which is permitted for the same reason it is on a District Magistrate in Sector 7: the accountability rests on STATUTORY OFFICE. Persons appointed under the Juvenile Justice Act and the POCSO framework carry personal legal duties in respect of a named child, enforceable in court. || [self_employment] Rare, and it is one of the few professions in Sectors 8 to 13 where that is true. Child protection authority derives from a statutory post or an accredited institution - there is no independent version of this work, and anyone offering one should be treated with suspicion. || [demand_signal] Moderate, and constrained by sanctioned posts rather than by need. District Child Protection Units are mandated nationally and are widely understaffed, which is a funding fact rather than a demand signal.
